name: 15-Minute Creamy Chipotle–Gorgonzola Sauce

ingredients.name: oyster mushrooms stems and caps, finely chopped
chipotle chilis, canned in adobo sauce, finely chopped, or more to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions.primary_message: In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add mushrooms, garlic, and thyme. Cook, stirring frequently, until mixture is very fragrant and mushrooms are tender and starting to brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in chipotle peppers. Add white wine and cook until it’s reduced by half, about 1 minute.

Slowly pour in heavy cream, stirring well to prevent scorching. Bring mixture to a simmer, then quickly reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Add Gorgonzola and cook, stirring frequently, until cheese has melted and sauce is thick and creamy, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat and season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in chopped parsley and a pinch of grated nutmeg, if using. Transfer to a serving bowl or spoon over meats and vegetables.

schema_metadata.keywords: cream sauce, steak sauce, cheese sauce, cheesy sauce, blue cheese sauce, chipotle sauce

description: This punchy, creamy chipotle–blue cheese sauce with smoky heat and savory funk is perfect for spooning over steak or roasted vegetables.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Chopped fresh parsley leaves, for serving (optional); Freshly grated nutmeg, for serving (optional)

Notes: Oyster mushrooms work especially well here due to their tenderness and quick cooking time, but any mushrooms, such as white button, cremini, or shiitake, can be used instead.
Gorgonzola works best here, as its higher fat content helps it melt smoothly into the cream.
Avoid using pre-crumbled Gorgonzola, which often contains anti-caking agents that can prevent it from melting smoothly into the sauce.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
Rewarm in a saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally as it warms and adding a splash of heavy cream to loosen the sauce as needed.
author: Kayla Simone Fowler
